title: E-Commerce Final Price
description: An e-commerce store offers a flat ₹100 discount on a purchase, followed by an 18% GST applied to the remaining amount. Calculate the final price.

guide.input: Drag an Input node, open ⚙ and set Input Data to 1500 (the original cart value).
mapping: Input → Subtract: open Subtract ⚙ and set Operand = 100 (flat discount).
Subtract → Multiply: set Operand = 1.18 (adds 18% GST to the remaining amount).
Multiply → Round: no settings needed (keeps 2 decimals).
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 1652.0.

title: Palindrome Check
description: Given a string, check if it reads the same backward as forward (a palindrome).
operation: Check if the string equals its reverse

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to radar.
mapping: Reverse → Compare (carries the reversed word). Open Compare ⚙ and set Operator = ==.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show True (a palindrome).

title: Restaurant Bill Split
description: A group receives a restaurant bill. Add a 10% tip to the total amount, then divide it equally among 4 friends to find each person's share.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to 2000 (total bill).
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 550.0.

title: Hashtag Generator
description: Convert a topic phrase into a valid single-word social media hashtag by removing all spaces, converting the text to uppercase, and adding # at the beginning.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to " python coding " (keep the spaces at both ends; quotes are optional).
mapping: Input → Replace: open Replace ⚙, Find = one space character, Replace With = empty (delete the text in the box).
guide.output: Set the Output format to #{value}. Run Flow must show #PYTHONCODING.

title: Server Temperature Alert
description: A server monitoring tool tracks system temperature. Convert the reading from Fahrenheit to Celsius, then check if the temperature exceeds the safe threshold of 40°C. Formula: C = (F - 32) * 5 / 9.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to 113 (temperature in °F).
mapping: Multiply → Divide: Operand = 9 (the value is now the Celsius reading, 45).
Divide → Compare: set Operator = > and Value = 40 (safe threshold).
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show True (45°C > 40°C).

title: Swap Locker Numbers
description: Two students are assigned the wrong locker numbers. Create a workflow that swaps Student A and Student B's locker numbers.
expected_output:
Student A locker = 25
Student B locker = 12

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to the JSON {"student_a_locker": 12, "student_b_locker": 25}.
mapping: Input → Output (one connection). The swap happens in the Output format, where A takes B's value and B takes A's.
guide.output: Set the Output format to: Student A locker = {value[student_b_locker]}\nStudent B locker = {value[student_a_locker]}  (type \n where the line break goes). Run Flow must show the two swapped lines.

title: Employee Performance & Bonus Evaluator
description: An HR evaluation tool computes employee monthly bonuses based on score ratings and extra project hours. Base Bonus = Extra Hours * $25. If Rating >= 4.5, double the base bonus (* 2.0); otherwise keep it unchanged (* 1.0). Add a fixed $100 attendance allowance to the final evaluated bonus.
operation: Bonus = (Extra Hours * 25) * multiplier (2.0 if Rating >= 4.5 else 1.0) + 100

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"employee_name": "Sarah", "rating_score": 4.8, "extra_hours": 10}.
mapping: Branch 1 (base bonus): Input → Get (Key = extra_hours) → Multiply (Operand = 25).
Branch 2 (rating multiplier): Input → Get (Key = rating_score) → IfElse (Operator = >=, Value = 4.5, Then = 2, Otherwise = 1).
Merge: connect Multiply (branch 1) → a second Multiply node, then IfElse → the same second Multiply (it multiplies base bonus × multiplier; leave its Operand alone).
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must show 600.0.

title: School Supplies Budget
description: Calculate the total bill and check whether the student can afford it.

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"budget": 200, "notebook": 80, "pen": 30, "pencil_box": 100}.
mapping: Input → Get #1: Key = notebook,pen,pencil_box (comma-separated, no spaces) → Sum (total bill = 210).
Subtract inputs, in this order: connect Sum → Subtract FIRST, then Get #2 (budget) → Subtract SECOND (210 − 200 = 10).
guide.output: Set the Output format to Budget exceeded by {value}. Run Flow must show Budget exceeded by 10.

title: World Landmark Locator
description: A geography exploration tool identifies a famous world landmark. Given the landmark's name, look up its country and continent from a predefined dataset, determine its hemisphere position (Eastern if longitude >= 0, Northern if latitude >= 0), and render a Location Photo Card showing the landmark's image pinned on a simplified world map.
operation: Lookup country/continent/coordinates; classify hemisphere; render map pin and photo card
expected_output: Country: France | Continent: Europe | Hemisphere: Northern & Eastern Hemisphere

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to Eiffel Tower (the landmark name).
mapping: Input → Lookup (finds Country, Continent and coordinates in the predefined table).
Lookup → Hemisphere (longitude ≥ 0 = Eastern, latitude ≥ 0 = Northern; combines both).
guide.output: Set the Output format to Country: {value[country]} | Continent: {value[continent]} | Hemisphere: {value[hemisphere]}. Run Flow must show Country: France | Continent: Europe | Hemisphere: Northern & Eastern Hemisphere. The reference picture shows the map pin and photo card the tool would draw.

title: Weekly Attendance Chart
description: A class teacher wants to visualize the attendance of students over five days. Create a line chart using the attendance data, with days on the X-axis, number of students present on the Y-axis, and the chart title "Weekly Attendance".
operation: Plot attendance per day as a line chart
expected_output: Line chart titled 'Weekly Attendance' with days on the X-axis and students present on the Y-axis

guide.input: Drag an Input node and set Input Data to {"x": ["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday"], "y": [35,38,36,40,37]} (x = days, y = students present).
mapping: Input → LineChart: open LineChart ⚙ and set Title = Weekly Attendance, X Axis Label = Day, Y Axis Label = Students Present.
guide.output: Leave the Output format empty. Run Flow must draw the chart titled Weekly Attendance (days on X, students present on Y).
